references.text: The midwives feared God and did not obey Pharaoh's command, which provides context for their answer in verse 19.
Pharaoh's original command to the midwives to kill the Hebrew male infants, against which the midwives defend themselves here.
A midwife assists Rachel during a difficult birth, illustrating the role of the midwife in Hebrew tradition.
The Israelites were fruitful and became very numerous, supporting the midwives' claim about the vitality of Hebrew women.
Rebekah's birth of twins illustrates Hebrew women's childbirths in the time of the patriarchs.
A theological contrast between God's sovereignty over infertility (Gal) and supernatural fertility (Ex), both confirming His promise to make the people numerous.
